question: Which of the following Chola ruler built a temple for goddess Nishumbhasudini?
solution:
The correct answer is Vijayalaya.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Around the **ninth century AD, the Muttaraiyar**, a small main **dynasty**, ruled the **Kaveri delta.**
 
• They served the **Pallava kings of Kanchipuram** as their subjects.
 
• In the middle of the ninth century, **Vijayalaya**, a member of the ancient mainly **Chola family **from **Uraiyur**, conquered the delta from the **Muttaraiyar**.
 
• He created the town of **Thanjavur** as well as a shrine dedicated to **Nishumbhasudini**.
 
• The Chola empire was thought to have been founded by **Vijayalaya**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vijayalaya's** successors expanded the kingdom's borders by conquest, increasing its size and power.
 
• **Rajaraja** **I**, regarded as the most powerful Chola emperor, established control over the majority of the southern regions in 985 after ascending to the throne.
 
• **Rajendra I,** the son of **Rajaraja**, carried on his father's policies and even launched raids against the **Ganga valley, Sri Lanka**, and nations in** Southeast Asia** while building a navy to support these operations.
